:::{#exm-cartesian-product-many}
#### Three coin flips
<!-- no-figure: a list of eight outcomes; nothing to plot -->

Let $C = \set{H, T}$ be the faces of a coin.
The ways three flips can come out
form the [Cartesian product](#def-cartesian-product-many)
$C \times C \times C$,
whose elements are the eight $3$-[tuples](#def-tuple)

$$(H, H, H), (H, H, T), (H, T, H), (H, T, T), (T, H, H), (T, H, T), (T, T, H), (T, T, T).$$

For example, $(H, T, T)$ is heads on the first flip
and tails on the second and third.

:::
